title: The Hesiodic Creation (Cosmogony)
summary: In the Theogony, the first thing is Chaos, from which come Gaia (Earth), Tartarus, Eros, and Nyx. Gaia bears Ouranos (Sky), and the union of Gaia and Ouranos produces the Titans, the Cyclopes, and the Hecatoncheires [S1].

variants.name: Orphic
variants.description: A cosmic egg and the god Phanes; a different, later cosmogony [S5].

uncertainty_notes: The Orphic cosmogony (egg, Phanes) is a genuine alternative to the Hesiodic account; both are preserved [S1][S5].

chapters.heading: Chaos First
chapters.body: The first thing was Chaos, the yawning gap [S1].

chapters.heading: Gaia and the First Beings
chapters.body: From Chaos came Gaia, Tartarus, Eros, and Nyx [S1].

chapters.heading: Ouranos and the Titans
chapters.body: Gaia bore Ouranos; their union produced the Titans, Cyclopes, and Hecatoncheires [S1].

title: The Overthrow of Ouranos
summary: Ouranos imprisoned his children in Tartarus. Gaia, grieving, forged a flint sickle and set Cronus to castrate and overthrow him; the Erinyes and (in the Theogony) Aphrodite arose from his severed parts [S1].
uncertainty_notes: The origin of Aphrodite from Ouranos's severed member (Theogony) vs. her birth from Zeus & Dione (Iliad) is a genuine variant [S1][S2].

chapters.heading: The Imprisonment
chapters.body: Ouranos cast his children into Tartarus [S1].

chapters.heading: The Sickle
chapters.body: Gaia forged a sickle and set Cronus against him [S1].

chapters.heading: The Fall
chapters.body: Cronus castrated Ouranos, who retreated to the heavens [S1].

title: The Titanomachy (War of the Titans)
summary: Zeus, grown, forced Cronus to disgorge his siblings, freed the Cyclopes and Hecatoncheires, and led them to war against the Titans. After a great battle, the Titans were defeated and cast into Tartarus [S1].

chapters.heading: The Stone for Zeus
chapters.body: Rhea gave Cronus a wrapped stone in place of the infant Zeus [S1][S5].

chapters.heading: The Disgorging
chapters.body: Zeus forced Cronus to vomit up his swallowed siblings [S1].

chapters.heading: The War
chapters.body: With the Cyclopes and Hecatoncheires, Zeus defeated the Titans [S1].

chapters.heading: The Division
chapters.body: Zeus took the sky, Poseidon the sea, Hades the underworld [S1].

title: The Birth of Athena
summary: Zeus swallowed Metis, pregnant with their child, to avert the prophecy that the child would overthrow him. Athena was born fully formed and armored from Zeus's head [S1][S4][S5].
uncertainty_notes: Her mother is Metis in the Theogony and Iliad (a variant gives Dione) [S1][S2].

chapters.heading: The Prophecy
chapters.body: A child of Metis would overthrow Zeus [S1][S5].

chapters.heading: The Swallowing
chapters.body: Zeus swallowed Metis while pregnant [S1].

chapters.heading: The Birth
chapters.body: Athena sprang from Zeus's head, fully armed [S4][S5].

title: Athena and Poseidon for Athens
summary: Athena and Poseidon each offered a gift to the city: she the olive tree, he the sea (or a horse). The city chose Athena's gift, and she became its patron [S5][S6].
uncertainty_notes: A civic aition (origin story), not a battle; the 'gifts' differ slightly across sources [S5][S6].

chapters.heading: The Contest
chapters.body: Both gods offered a gift to the new city [S5].

chapters.heading: The Gifts
chapters.body: Athena gave the olive; Poseidon the sea/spring [S5][S6].

chapters.heading: The Choice
chapters.body: The city chose Athena, who became its patron [S6].

title: The Birth of Aphrodite (Two Accounts)
summary: In the Theogony, Aphrodite is born from the sea-foam around Ouranos's severed member at Cythera. In the Iliad, she is the daughter of Zeus and Dione. Both accounts are canonical and incompatible [S1][S2].
uncertainty_notes: These are genuinely incompatible accounts; we present both, not a merge [S1][S2].

chapters.heading: Theogony Version
chapters.body: Sea-foam from Ouranos's severed member [S1].

chapters.heading: Iliad Version
chapters.body: Daughter of Zeus and Dione [S2].

title: The Abduction of Persephone and the Seasons
summary: Hades abducted Persephone to be his queen. Demeter's grief withheld the earth's fertility until a compromise: Persephone spends part of the year on earth (spring/summer) and part in the underworld (autumn/winter), because she ate pomegranate seeds below [S4][S5].
uncertainty_notes: The pomegranate-seed detail is from later/Orphic tradition, not the Homeric Hymn to Demeter [S4][S5].

chapters.heading: The Abduction
chapters.body: Hades took Persephone from a meadow [S4][S5].

chapters.heading: The Grief
chapters.body: Demeter's sorrow made the earth barren [S4][S5].

chapters.heading: The Compromise
chapters.body: Persephone divides the year between earth and underworld [S4][S5].

chapters.heading: The Pomegranate
chapters.body: Six pomegranate seeds bound her to return (later/Orphic detail) [S4][S5].

title: Perseus and Medusa
summary: Sent to fetch Medusa's head, Perseus was aided by Athena (mirror-shield) and Hermes (winged sandals, sickle); he beheaded the Gorgon, and Pegasus and Chrysaor sprang from her blood [S1][S5].
uncertainty_notes: The 'beautiful maiden' Medusa is Ovid's later version; Hesiod's Gorgons are monstrous from birth [S1][S5].

chapters.heading: The Quest
chapters.body: Polydectes sent Perseus for Medusa's head [S5].

chapters.heading: The Gifts
chapters.body: Athena's shield, Hermes's sandals and sickle [S5].

chapters.heading: The Slaying
chapters.body: Perseus beheaded Medusa via the mirror [S5].

chapters.heading: Pegasus
chapters.body: Pegasus and Chrysaor sprang from her blood [S1][S5].

title: Typhon and Zeus
summary: Typhon, the greatest monster, warred against the gods and wounded Zeus, who was cut and fell. Zeus recovered, regained his thunderbolt, and buried Typhon under Mount Etna [S1][S5].
uncertainty_notes: The Typhon passage in the Theogony is a later interpolation [S1].

chapters.heading: The Monster
chapters.body: Typhon, hundred-headed, born of Gaia [S1].

chapters.heading: The Wounding
chapters.body: Typhon cut Zeus and made him fall [S1].

chapters.heading: The Burial
chapters.body: Zeus buried Typhon under Etna; its fires are his breath [S1][S5].

title: The Twelve Labors of Heracles
summary: Driven to madness by Hera, Heracles killed his children and was set to perform the twelve labors for Eurystheus as penance — including the Nemean lion, the Lernaean Hydra, and the capture of Cerberus. After his death he was raised to Olympus [S5].

chapters.heading: The Madness
chapters.body: Hera drove Heracles to kill his children [S5].

chapters.heading: The Labors
chapters.body: Twelve tasks for Eurystheus [S5].

chapters.heading: Cerberus
chapters.body: The final labor: capture Cerberus [S5].

chapters.heading: Olympus
chapters.body: After his death he was raised to Olympus [S5].

title: Odysseus and the Cyclops
summary: On his way home from Troy, Odysseus was trapped by the Cyclops Polyphemus, whom he blinded and escaped by calling himself 'Nobody' (Outis), so the other Cyclopes did not come when they heard 'Nobody is doing this' [S3].

chapters.heading: The Cave
chapters.body: Odysseus's men were trapped by Polyphemus [S3].

chapters.heading: The Blinding
chapters.body: Odysseus blinded the Cyclops with a stake [S3].

chapters.heading: 'Nobody'
chapters.body: He called himself Outis (Nobody) to outwit the others [S3].

chapters.heading: The Wrath
chapters.body: Poseidon (Polyphemus's father) cursed Odysseus's journey home [S3].
